title: Copy List With Random Pointer
description:
A linked list is given where each node carries an extra random pointer, which may point at any node in the list or at None.

Return a deep copy of the list. Every next and random pointer in your copy must point at a node in the copy, in the same arrangement as the original.

class Node:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None, random=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        self.random = random

The list is given as [[val, random_index], ...], where random_index is the position the random pointer targets, or null for None. Your answer is serialized back into the same form.

Returning the list you were given is rejected — the copy is the exercise.

Constraints:

  • The list holds between 0 and 1000 nodes.
  • -10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4.
  • random is None or points at a node in the list.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Random pointers reach forwards, backwards and to None within the same list.
Both nodes point their random at the second node.
